Units of covered investment contracts offered

Number of units of covered investment contract offered, in the unit the issuer defines. Rule 101(e)(1) as proposed makes one unit of a covered investment contract one unit of the subject crypto asset; Auditchain Labs recommends that an issuer be permitted to define the unit as a functional unit - the subject crypto asset together with the software or other technical primitives the crypto asset invokes (for Pacioli.ai, a Pacioli Validating Node of 50,000 AUDT with its node software license) - with the Rule 101(e) measures reported alongside in the functional-unit elements. Where the unit is the crypto asset itself, the two agree.
Purchase price per unit

Price per unit of the covered investment contract, in the unit the issuer defines (see UnitsOfCoveredInvestmentContractsOffered). Rule 101(e)(2) as proposed determines it by reference to the price per unit of the subject crypto asset; that measure is reported in EquivalentPurchasePricePerUnitOfSubjectCryptoAsset. If a price range is given, report the midpoint.

Functional unit of covered investment contract and Rule 101(e) equivalents [abstract]

Proposed by Auditchain Labs; not required by the proposed rule. Auditchain Labs recommends (Requests for Comment 6, 7 and 31) that an issuer may define the unit of a covered investment contract as a functional unit: the subject crypto asset together with the software or other technical primitives the crypto asset invokes and that an institution needs to stand up and operate the network (for Pacioli.ai, a Pacioli Validating Node of 50,000 AUDT with its node software license). The elements below carry the crypto-asset content of each unit and the measures Rule 101(e) as proposed would report, so the Commission can read the offering either way and the per-crypto-asset arithmetic can be checked. The recommendation is intended to make the exemption easier to use for building real utility than for a token sale with nothing behind it.
Units of subject crypto asset in each unit of covered investment contract

Proposed by Auditchain Labs; not required by the proposed rule. The number of units of the subject crypto asset delivered with each unit of covered investment contract as the issuer defines the unit. 1 where the unit is the crypto asset itself.
Equivalent units of subject crypto asset offered (Rule 101(e)(1) measure)

Proposed by Auditchain Labs; not required by the proposed rule. Units of covered investment contract offered times units of the subject crypto asset per unit: the number of units Rule 101(e)(1) as proposed would count.
Equivalent purchase price per unit of subject crypto asset (Rule 101(e)(2) measure)

Proposed by Auditchain Labs; not required by the proposed rule. Purchase price per unit divided by units of the subject crypto asset per unit: the price per unit Rule 101(e)(2) as proposed would report.
Purchasers limited to accredited investors

Proposed by Auditchain Labs; not required by the proposed rule. True if the issuer restricts the offering to accredited investors as defined in Rule 501 of Regulation D, a qualification for purchasers under Rule 103(b)(2)(i); where true, the 10 percent investment limit of Rule 300(c)(2)(i)(C) does not operate because every purchaser is accredited.

Proposed by Auditchain Labs; not required by the proposed rule. Why a post-qualification amendment is filed. Rule 301(f)(2) says when one must be filed; saying which reason applies lets the 12-month deadline be checked.
Qualification date of the offering statement

Proposed by Auditchain Labs; not required by the proposed rule. In a special financial report, the date the Commission qualified the offering statement (Rule 305(a)(2)(ii)). In a post-qualification amendment, the most recent qualification date: the offering statement or the last post-qualification amendment (Rule 301(f)(2)). The forms do not ask for it, but these deadlines run from it. In an offering circular filed under Rule 302(f)(1) or (3), the later of the qualification date of the offering statement and that of a post-qualification amendment containing an offering circular; the omitted pricing information is filed within 15 business days after it (Rule 302(c)).

Merkle root method [domain]
Reg CA filing merkle tree, version 1 [member]

Proposed by Auditchain Labs; not required by the proposed rule. Each fact is written as a JSON object with the keys concept, entity, period, dimensions, unit, decimals and value, leaving out keys with no value; concepts, dimensions and members are written as namespace, "#" and local name, and a typed dimension by its value. The object is serialized under RFC 8785 (JSON Canonicalization Scheme). Each leaf is SHA-256 (FIPS 180-4) of the byte 0x00 followed by that serialization; the leaves are sorted in ascending order and combined into the Merkle Tree Hash of RFC 6962, section 2.1. Left out of the root: the root itself, this method and every fact in the table of anchors.
